text:
SRE-Bot: 🚨 ALERT gpu-hotpool-rc-3: GPU utilization 96% over 5m, queue depth increasing (+4.8k reqs), 429-rate 18% across hotpath routes. Autoscaler heartbeat lagging. Paging on-call.
Maya (oncall): I'm on it, taking pager. Will post updates here. Estimating initial triage 5m.
Dana (support): customers reporting elevated 429s in EU and us-west. Support ticket count spiking to 26. Not yet widespread-but-noticeable.
Priya (runtime): initial feeling: autoscaler didn't spawn extra hot GPUs because rateclass allocation mismatched after last routing change. Seeing 'allocation rejected: reserved-capacity-check' in autoscaler logs.
Jorge (platform): I can access autoscaler logs and cluster metrics. @Maya do you want me to bump the pool manually while we triage config?
Maya (oncall): Yes please, manual scale to +4 GPUs for hotpool and set idle timeout to 5m. That should buy time. Also flip tokenbucket regen to 2x for hotpath to absorb burst.
Jorge (platform): executing now:
```
# scale command
kubectl patch gpupool hotpool-rc-3 -p '{"spec":{"replicas":12}}' --type=merge
```
Deploy-Bot: Deploy queued: patch applied to hotpool-rc-3, controller acknowledged.
Jorge (platform): manual scale took, new nodes joining (3/4 registered). Queue depth flatlining. 429 rate still elevated but trending down from 18% -> 11%.
Priya (runtime): digging into autoscaler heartbeat, found repeated `HeartbeatTimeout` and `RateclassMismatch` entries around 4695012280. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:xxZ] autoscaler: HeartbeatTimeout pool=hotpool-rc-3 last_heartbeat=47s
[2026-03-15T09:12:xxZ] autoscaler: Allocation rejected: rateclass=prod-hot -> target-tier=fast but tokenbucket-tier=standard
```
Maya (oncall): That matches the recent rollout where we changed some user routing to 'fast' tier but didn't update tokenbucket mappings. Can we revert that rollout?
Jorge (platform): I pushed a rollback flag minutes ago against the routing change (rollout id: r-8921). Confirmed rollback started.
Priya (runtime): autoscaler still reading stale rateclass map from config-store due to caching TTL. I can force reload: `curl -X POST http://config-internal/reload?service=autoscaler`
Maya (oncall): Go ahead Priya. Also please increase tokenbucket units temporarily for hotpath: `hotpool: units=2000 -> 8000` for 10m.
Priya (runtime): applied reload and tokenbucket bump. Patch:
```
POST /admin/tokenbucket/hotpath {"units":8000,"regen_ms":1000}
```
SRE-Bot: NOTE: circuit breaker engaged for fallback tier at 09:12:54 UTC. Fallback routing is healthy.
Dana (support): after manual scale + tokenbucket bump, support tickets per min dropped from 6/min -> 1/min. Customers still see intermittent 429s but many are recovered. Updating ticket statuses.
Maya (oncall): Summary so far: cause = rateclass/tokenbucket misconfig after rollout + autoscaler heartbeat lag -> autoscaler refused allocations -> pool saturation -> queue growth -> 429s. Immediate mitigations: manual scale, tokenbucket bump, rollback routing change, force config reload.
Jorge (platform): Observed autoscaler pods OOM at 09:11:15 on one replica; restarted and rejoined. Need to check if OOM caused heartbeat lag. Heap growth correlated with config map watch backlog.
Priya (runtime): Confirmed one autoscaler pod OOM. Logs show GC thrashing on large rateclass map. We should trim map size or increase memory for autoscaler. Temporary mitigation: restart policy set to aggressive (restartLimit=3) and increase memory to 2Gi.
Maya (oncall): Let's make those temporary changes now. Jorge, can you handle mem bump? Priya, can you open a follow-up to audit rateclass map growth?
Jorge (platform): On it — patching the deployment: `resources.limits.memory=2Gi`. Applying now.
Deploy-Bot: Deployment autopatcher applied: autoscaler replicas restarted with updated resources.
Jorge (platform): autoscaler pods are stable again, heartbeats normal. 429s down to 3%. Queue draining.
Dana (support): Customer impact: 26 tickets opened, 5 paywalled customers saw degraded SLA during 09:08-09:22 UTC window. I started priority outreach to those 5.
Maya (oncall): Good. We'll keep scaled pool for 20m then let autoscaler handle downscale after verifying stability.
Priya (runtime): Postmortem notes to capture: 1) rollout changed routing without tokenbucket mapping update, 2) autoscaler memory too low for map size, 3) missing integration test for rollout+tokenbucket consistency.
Jorge (platform): Action items (quick):
- `CH1` Increase autoscaler mem permanently and add OOM alert (owner: Jorge)
- `CH2` Add preflight check in rollout pipeline to validate rateclass <-> tokenbucket mapping (owner: Priya)
- `CH3` Add test that simulates sustained heartbeat lag with queue growth (owner: Maya)
- `CH4` Post-incident customer outreach (owner: Dana)
Maya (oncall): I'll file the incident and set severity to Sev2 since some customers hit SLA. Priya, please draft a short technical summary for the postmortem. Everyone please add notes to the incident doc: https://internal.redwood/ops/incidents/4695012345 (runbook link).
Dana (support): I'll update the five impacted customers with timeline and mitigations.
Priya (runtime): One more datapoint: tokenbucket config had regen_ms=5000 previously (too slow). We bumped to 1000ms; will evaluate if 2k better after analysis.
Maya (oncall): Closing on-call thread: leaving a handoff to the morning shift (Jorge) for follow up. I will handover at 09:45 UTC.
Jorge (platform): Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye on autoscaler mem and queued requests.
SRE-Bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> warm-standby. Logging incident for postmortem.
Maya (oncall): Final note: temporary changes expire in 30m unless owners extend. If anything regresses, @pager escalate to eng-sre. :white_check_mark:
